messages.subject: Tomas Sieger
messages.body_plain:
Hey, should we add Tomas as a group member? It looks like he would be a valuable contributor!

-----------

Dear Di, thanks for the info.
Just for curiosity, would you (cranvas) possibly accept pull requests?
Maybe, I will be missing something in cranvas in the meantime and will
try to implement it.
I like cranvas (and ggobi) very much, using it in my research.

BTW I wrote idendro, an interactive dendrogram for R (as a Google
Summer of Code project last year), which is based on
qtpaint/qtbase/plumbr and "bidirectionally" integrates with cranvas in
terms of live bindings over mutaframes, such that you can i) color
clustered data both in dendro and in feature space projections in
cranvas, and ii) see (in dendro) which data get brushed data in
cranvas plots. You can take a look at
https://github.com/tsieger/idendro, e.g. idendroCranvasDemo. idendro
is still under development, but should work, in general. (Any comments
would be highly welcome.)

cheers,
Tomas
---------------------------
Di Cook
vis...@gmail.com

messages.subject: Build on R 3.0.0
messages.body_plain:
Everyone,

I'm trying to build qtbase for the latest version of R on the Mac. Has anyone done this? I am getting this error, which looks like it might be having trouble finding the Qt libraries? (Working from RStudio, install from git, but I get the same error trying to install from the command line in a terminal window.)

Error : .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'qtbase', details:
  call: dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...)
  error: unable to load shared object '/Users/dicook/Library/R/3.0/library/qtbase/libs/qtbase.so':
  dlopen(/Users/dicook/Library/R/3.0/library/qtbase/libs/qtbase.so, 6): Library not loaded: libQtCLucene.4.dylib
  Referenced from: /Library/Frameworks/QtHelp.framework/Versions/4/QtHelp
  Reason: image not found
Error: loading failed
Execution halted
ERROR: loading failed
* removing ‘/Users/dicook/Library/R/3.0/library/qtbase’

cheers,
Di
---------------------------
Di Cook
vis...@gmail.com

Michael

messages.subject: Re: cranvas on Windows? (2nd turn)
messages.body_plain:
Dear Michael,
 any update on the Windows story, please?
 Any time estimates?

I'm sorry for just keeping asking...
(I'm finishing a paper on my package based on qt* and would like to
mention installation dependencies there. Also, I tend to think that
the fact that cranvas does not run on Windows poses a serious drawback
that restricts wider adoption of cranvas, which is unfortunate these
days given the outbreak of web-based interactive visualization
frameworks on one side, and all the effort put in qt*, cranvas etc. on
the other side.)

cheers,
 Tomas

On Sun, Jul 15, 2012 at 1:08 AM, Michael Lawrence <law...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Current status is that it's working on my computer on both 32 bit and 64
> bit. I had to build 64 bit Qt from scratch, because there is no existing 64
> bit MinGW (gcc) binary. Unfortunately, Qt binaries are not easily
> relocatable: the build path is embedded in the binary. The Nokia installers
> modify the binaries during installation. I requested that the CRAN
> maintainers build their own Qt so that the paths are right for their system.
> They have refused to do that so far. If they don't, I'll have to do
> something like make my own installers through reverse engineering the Nokia
> installer, or write some sort of script that attempts to rename the symbols
> in the MSVC DLLs so that they link with MinGW binaries.
>
> Michael

messages.subject: Re: cranvas on Windows? (2nd turn)
messages.body_plain:
I have been focusing on getting support for Qt 5, but I'm not making much progress (the smoke generator is yielding garbage). Apparently, Qt 5.1 will have official installers for Windows. I did find though that there is a new qtbinpatcher utility that should make it easy to install binaries manually, and there are Qt 4.8.4 binaries available in a zip archive.

I will have to try that in a Windows VM to see what happens.
